classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equal radii and vertically opposite angles as SAS data, then choose corresponding alternate angles to prove parallelism. The question supplies both triangle pairs and the concluding route.

content.prompt: The line segments $AOC$ and $BOD$ are diameters of two concentric circles with centre $O$. We will prove that $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

spec.description: Two concentric unfilled circles and their intersecting diameters. No quadrilateral sides are supplied.
spec.mathematics: A and C are opposite endpoints of the inner diameter; B and D are opposite endpoints of the outer diameter; O is the common centre.
spec.answerVisibility: Only circles, diameters and the five supplied labels are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle AOB\equiv\triangle COD$ and hence prove that $AB\parallel CD$.

answer.short: $\triangle AOB\equiv\triangle COD$ by SAS; equal alternate angles give $AB\parallel CD$.
answer.worked:
Join $AB$ and $CD$. In $\triangle AOB$ and $\triangle COD$:
$$\begin{align*}AO&=CO&&\text{(radii of the inner circle)}\\BO&=DO&&\text{(radii of the outer circle)}\\\angle AOB&=\angle COD&&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle AOB\equiv\triangle COD$ by SAS. Corresponding angles give $\angle ABO=\angle CDO$. These are alternate angles on transversal $BD$, so $AB\parallel CD$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle BOC\equiv\triangle DOA$ and hence prove that $BC\parallel DA$. Conclude that $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

answer.short: $\triangle BOC\equiv\triangle DOA$ by SAS; equal alternate angles give $BC\parallel DA$. Together with $AB\parallel CD$, this proves that $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked:
Join $BC$ and $DA$. In $\triangle BOC$ and $\triangle DOA$:
$$\begin{align*}BO&=DO&&\text{(radii of the outer circle)}\\CO&=AO&&\text{(radii of the inner circle)}\\\angle BOC&=\angle DOA&&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle BOC\equiv\triangle DOA$ by SAS. Corresponding angles give $\angle CBO=\angle ADO$. These are alternate angles on transversal $BD$, so $BC\parallel DA$.

Part a gives $AB\parallel CD$. Hence $ABCD$ has two pairs of parallel opposite sides and is a parallelogram.
